target.title: fix(codex): Pro model first turns fail when reasoning defaults to minimal
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running Codex Pro models (`gpt-5.5-pro` or `gpt-5.4-pro`) could have OpenClaw send the legacy `minimal` reasoning effort when an agent turn starts with the default thinking level. Those Pro models use the modern Codex reasoning enum, so the first app-server request can reject `minimal` instead of starting cleanly.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing modern Codex model detection already drives the `minimal` -> `low` translation for `gpt-5.5`, `gpt-5.4`, `gpt-5.4-mini`, and related modern ids. This change adds the two Pro ids to that source-of-truth predicate, leaving legacy and unknown model ids unchanged.

I also checked the current `origin/main` implementation and visible open PRs before submission: `origin/main` still lacked the Pro ids, and the only broad Codex reasoning PR found (#81300) changes reasoning summary plumbing rather than this reasoning-effort enum mapping.

## User Impact

Codex Pro agent turns that rely on the default/minimal thinking setting now prepare `low` reasoning effort before the app-server request, avoiding an invalid first request/retry path for those models.

## Evidence

Before the production change, the new focused regression failed for both Pro ids:

```text
expected 'minimal' to be 'low'
translates 'minimal' -> 'low' for gpt-5.5-pro so the first request is accepted
translates 'minimal' -> 'low' for gpt-5.4-pro so the first request is accepted
```

After the change:

```text
Validation `codex-reasoning-effort-pro-models` (pass, exit_code=0)

Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  28 passed | 51 skipped (79)
```

```text
Validation `codex-pro-runtime-probe` (pass, exit_code=0)

gpt-5.5-pro minimal -> low
gpt-5.4-pro minimal -> low
```

```text
Validation `codex-provider-tests` (pass, exit_code=0)

Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  21 passed (21)
```

A full live Codex Pro network turn was not run because it requires external Codex OAuth and Pro model entitlement. The runtime probe loads the production thread-lifecycle resolver directly and exercises the exact value that OpenClaw prepares before dispatching the Codex app-server request.
